Sarah Austin aged about 30 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married that she lived as a hired yearly Servant for 12 Months and upwards at the yearly Wages of Six Guineas that with a Mr. Dean who kept the Sign of the Bag of Nails at Pimliea in the Parish of Saint George Hanover Square in the County of Middlesex that she hath quitted said Service upwards of Two years since which time she has not lived as a hired yearly Servant for one year or done any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement And further saith that she has one Child living vizt. Sarah aged about 6 Months born a Bastard at the House of a Mr. Taylor in Houghton Street That George Bell a Soldier in the 1st. Regt. of Foot Guards is the Father thereof

Mark Houldins aged about 41 years upon his Oath saith that about 17 years ago he Intermarried with Elizth. his late Wife (who has been dead about Eight years) at the Parish Church of Saint Leonard Shoreditch and by whom he hath one Child living Vizt. Charlotte aged About 13 years that he Rented and lived in a House in Winchester Square in the Parish of Saint Mary Overys in Southwark for 6 Months or thereabouts at the yearly Rent of £14 that he hath quitted said House about 13 years ago since which time he has not Rented any House Tenement or Lodging of £10 a year paid Taxes or done any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement

Sarah Wilson aged about 33 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married that she lived as a hired yearly Servant with a Mr. Foot in Gloucester Street in the Parish of St. George the Martyr in the County of Middlesex for 15 Months or thereabouts at the yearly Wages of £6 that she hath quitted said Service about 4 Months since which time she hath done no Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement

Ann Owens aged about 27 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married that she lived as a hired yearly Servant with a Mrs. Lambert in Church Row Aldgate in the Parish of Saint Botoplh Botolph Aldgate in the City of London for 2 years & upwards at the yearly Wages of £6 that she hath quitted said Service about 3 years since which time she hath done no Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement.

Henry Snow aged about 22 years upon her Oath saith that he was placed out by Apprentice by the Churchwardens & Overseers of the Poor of the Parish of Saint George Hanover Square to a Mr. Harrison of the Edgware Road in the Parish of Saint Mary Le Bone in the County of Middlesex Hair Dresser for 5 years & 12 that he served One year and an half of the his said Apprenticeship that then his Master took him before Two Justices and had him Regularly discharged that since he left his said Master he has not lived as a hired yearly Servant for one year Rented House Tent. or Lodging of £10 a year paid Taxes or done any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement

Sarah Fisher aged about 33 years upon her Oath saith That she was bound an Apprentice by the Society of Cliffords Inn to a Mr. Patmore of the King Head in the Old Jewry Victualler for 7 years that she served about 3 years and an half of her said Apprenticeship and her Master not Treating her well she Applyed to the Society of Cliffords Inn and made her Complaint That upon such Complaint the said Society got her Discharged - That she has one Child living vizt. George aged about Five weeks not yet baptized

Alice Aylsworth alias Pritchard aged about 50 years upon her Oath saith that she Intermarried with John Aylsworth her late Husband at the Parish Church of Saint Sepulchres about 20 years ago That he has been dead about 4 years that he served his Time as an Apprentice to a Peruke Maker in Aldersgate Street in the Parish of Saint Botolph without Aldersgate in the County of Middlesex that after he was out of his said Apprenticeship he never did any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement

Nathaniel Whitcombe aged about 37 years upon his Oath saith that he lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr Bray in Mortimer Street Cavendish Square in the Parish of Saint Mary le born in the County of Middx for about three years at the yearly Wages of any turn Sixteen Guineas that he Quitted such Service about five years ago and since that time has not done any Act whereby to the best of his knowledge he may have acquired any subsequent Settlement

Edward Burbidge one of the Beadles of the Parish of Saint Clement Danes on behalf of Mary Pinnell who is at present ill Maketh Oath & Saith that he has been informed which information he believes to be true that the said Mary Pinnell intermarried with James Pinnell her prest. Husband at the Parish Church of Saint Andrew Holborn about Twenty one years ago that her said Husband Rented and lived in a House in Battle Bridge in the Parish of Saint James Clerkenwell in the County of Middlesex for Twelve Months and upwards at the yearly Rent of Twelve Pounds that after he quitted said House he never did any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement to the best of this Deponent knowledge Information or belief

Samuel Jones aged 34 years or thereabouts upon his Oath saith that his Father kept a House in Oxford Street in the Parish of Saint James Westminster was by Trade a Watch Maker That he this deponent went to reside with his Father there when 2 years of Age and lived there with him till he was about 12 years of Age that he lived in the same House with a Brother in Law about 5 years and learnt this Business of Painting of him that since he quitted said House he had done no Act matter of Thing whereby he may have gained a subsequent Settlement to the best of this Examinants knowledge and belief

Mary Barry aged about 30 years upon her Oath saith that in the Month of May 1787 she Intermarried with James Barry her present Husband at the Parish Church of Saint Martin in the fields that he has deserted this Examinant about Two Months That her said Husband informed this Examinant that his Settlement was in the Parish of Saint Dunstan in the West in the City of London by living Twelve Months and upwards as a hired yearly Servant with Mr. Cox who kept the Mitre Tavern in the said Parish of Saint Dunstan in the West in the City of London that after he was quitted said Service about he never did any Act to the best of this Examinants knowledge to gain a Subsequent Settlement that she hath Two Children living viz dilicet Diana and Mary both Twins born in the Month of January last And both by this Examinants Husband

William Penny aged about 48 years upon his Oath saith that about 25 years ago he Intermarried with Ann his present Wife at the Parish Church of Saint Martin in the fields that he this Examinant Rented and lived in a House in Cumberland Street in the Parish of Saint Pancras in the County of Middlesex for about Eighteen Months at the yearly Rent of Thir Twenty Six Pounds that he hath quitted said House about Sixteen years since which time he has not Rented any House Tenement or Lodging of Ten Pounds a year paid Taxes or done any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement

Winifred Arthur aged about 23 years upon her Oath saith That she never was married Rented House or paid Taxes that she lived as a hired yearly Servant with a Mr. Moore at Stoke Newington in the Parish of Hornsey in the County of Middlesex for Three years or thereabouts at the yearly Wages of Four Pounds that she hath quitted said Service about Five years ago since which time she hath not lived as a hired yearly Servant for one year or done any Act Matter or Thing to gain Subsequent Settlement

Elizabeth Tring aged about 31 years upon her Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as a hired yearly Servant with for 12 Months and upwards at the King of Prussia's Head in Wych Street in the Parish of Saint Clement Danes in the County of Middlesex That since she quitted said Service she never did any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement That she hath One Child living vizt. William aged about 9 years born a Bastard at the Bull and Gate in Holborn in the Parish of Saint Giles in the fields in the County of Middlesex

Margarett Dowlin aged about 26 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married that she lived as a hired yearly Servant with Mr. Foster in Richmond Buildings in the Parish of Saint Anne in the Liberty of Westminster upwards of Twelve Months at the yearly Wages of Six Pounds that she hath quitted said Service upwards of Two years since which time she has done no Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement

Ann Barden aged 28 yrs. or thereabouts upon her Oath Saith that she never was Married Rented House or paid Taxes that she never lived as a hired yearly Servant for one year That some time since she this Examinant was removed by an Order of Removal from the Parish of Saint Clement Danes to the Parish of Saint Ann Blackfryars that being the place of her legal Settlement by Virtue of her Father and that she this Examinant is poor and unable to maintain herself.

Sarah Brawn aged about 21 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married that she lived as a hired yearly Servant with a Mrs. Laverock in King Johns Square in the Parish of Saint Mary Magdalen Bermondsey in the County of Surry for Twelve Months at the yearly Wages of Seven Guineas that she hath quitted said Service in the Month of June last since which time she has done no Act to gain a subsequent Settlement

Rebecca Spencer aged about 32 years on behalf of Mary Groves Maketh Oath and Saith that the said Mary Groves was bound an Apprentice to this Examt. about 20 Months ago that she this Examt. not being able to support the said Mary Groves applied to a Justice and got her discharged that the last Forty days Servitude under the said Indre was at No. 10 Great Queen Street in the Parish of Saint Giles in the fields in the County of Middlesex

Benjamin Newman one of the Beadles of the Parish of Saint Clement Danes on behalf of Michael aged upwards of Three years and Mary aged about Eighteen Months Two Infants Maketh Oath and Saith that he has been informed which Information he verily believes to be true that the said Two Infants were both born Bastards on the Body of Jane Wheeler in the House of a Mr. Stevens the corner of Bear Yard Lincolns Inn Fields in the Parish of Saint Giles in the fields in the County of Middlesex

Ann Steppen aged about 28 years upon her Oath saith that she intermarried with Wm. Steppen her present Husband (who is at present insane) at the Parish Church of Walcot in the City of Bath that her said Husband Rented and lived in a Two Rooms in Pemberton Row in the Parish of Saint Brides alias Bridgett the City of London for Six Months or thereabouts at the yearly Rent of Twelve Pounds that he hath quitted said Place about Twelve Months since which time he has done no Act to gain a subsequent Settlement

Mary Barry aged about 30 years upon her Oath saith that about Fourteen Months ago she Intermarried with James Barry her present Husband at the Parish Church of Saint Martin in the fields that her said Husband has deserted this Examinant about Four Months that she has Two Children living by her said Husband vizt. Diana and Mary both Turns born in the Month of January last that she this Examinant and her Two Children in the Month of June last past were passed from this Parish to the Parish of Saint Dunstan in the west upon the information of her Husband that he lived Twelve Months and upwards with Mr. Cox in Mitre Court Fleet Street in the Said Parish of Saint Dunstan as a hired yearly Servant that this Examt. has does not know where her said Husband was born whether he served any Apprenticeship Rented House Tenement on Lodging of £10 a year paid Taxes or where he belonged that the said Parish of Saint Dunstan Appealed against the said Order of Remove and proved that he was a weekly Servant with Mr. Cox Strange and not a yearly Servant whereupon the Sessions quashed the Order and this Examinant further On her Oath Saith that before she Intermarried with James Barry she lived as a hired yearly Servant with Miss Lock in Bedford Street Covent Garden in the Parish of Saint Paul Covent Garden in the County of Middlesex for Three years and upwards at the yearly Wages of seven Guineas that she hath quitted said Service upwards of Two years since which time she has done no Act to gain a except so intermarrying with the said James Barry above letter she not being is above Stated Subsequent Settlement

Sarah Morrell aged about 33 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married That she lived as a hired yearly Servant with a Mr. Branches a Brushmaker the corner of Buckingham Street in the Parish of Saint Martin in the fields for Two years or thereabouts at the yearly Wages of £4 that she hath quitted said Service about Seven Months since which time she hath done No Act to gain a subsequent Settlement

Pauls in the City of London that she hath Quitted said Service about Three years since which time she hath Not lived as a hired yearly Servant for Twelve Months nor ever Rented any house Tenement on Lodging of Ten Pounds a Year Paid Taxes or done any Act to gain a subsequent Settlement

Mary Partridge Aged about Twenty six Years Upon her Oath Saith that she never was married that she lived as a hired Yearly Servant at Mr. Calverts in New Street Covent Garden in the parish of St. Martin in the Fields in the County of Middlesex for about 7 Years at the Yearly Wages of 8 & 12 Quas. that she hath quitted said Service about four Years; since which time she has not lived as a hired Yearly Servant for one Year or done any Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement to the best of this Examinant Knowledge information And belief

Elizabeth Close aged about 26 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married Rented House Tenement or Lodging of Ten Pounds a year or paid Taxes that she lived as a hired yearly Servant with one Mr. Werrip who kept the Spread Eagle Tavern in the Strand in the Parish of Saint Mary Le Strand in the Liberty of Westminster for about Two years at the yearly Wages of Six Pounds that she hath quitted said Service about Seven years ago since which time she hath not lived as a hired Yearly Servant for one year or done any Act to gain a subsequent Settlement

Mary Best aged about Twenty years upon her Oath saith that she never was married Rented House Tenement or Lodging of Ten pounds a year paid Taxes lived as a hired yearly Servant for Twelve Months or ever bound an Apprentice That she has been informed by Elizabeth Barber this Examinant Mother which Information she verily believes to be true That Richard Best this Examinants late father Rented and lived in a house in Long Alley Moorfields in the Parish of Saint Leonard Shoreditch in the County of Middlesex for about four years at the yearly Rent of Fourteen Guineas and that after her said late Father quitted said house he never did any Act to the best of this Examinants knowledge Information or belief whereby he might have gained a subsequent Settlement

William Giffard aged about 60 years upon his Oath saith that about 36 years ago her Intermarried with Elizabeth Carr (who has been dead about Twelve years) at the Parish Church of Medburn in Leicestershire by whom he hath Six Children living vizt. Wm. aged about 27 years Alice aged about 30 years Thomas aged about 20 years Sarah aged about 19 years and Mary aged about 17 years all provided for and Ann aged about 15 years unprovided for That he this Examinant Rented and lived in a house at Narrow Wall Lambeth Walk in the Parish of Saint Mary at Lambeth in the County of Surry for Six Months Years and upwards at the Yearly Rent of Ten Pounds that he hath done no Act since he quitted said house to gain a Subsequent Settlement and this Examinant further saith that his Daughter Ann never was bound an Apprentice lived as a hired yearly Servant for one year or done any Act to gain a Settlement in his own right

Ann Redhead aged about 57 years upon her Oath saith that she never was married That she lived as a hired yearly Servant with Mr. Joseph Laver who was a Sheriff Officer in Chancery Lane in the Liberty of the Rolls in the County of Middx for Three years and upwards at the yearly Wages of Five Pounds that she hath quitted said Service about Ten years since which time she has not lived as a hired yearly Servant for Twelve Months or done any Act to gain a subsequent Settlement

James Talboys one of the Beadles of the parish of Saint Clement Danes on behalf of Adam Marcham an Infant aged five Years and upwards Maketh Oath and Saith that he has been credibly informed which Information he verily believes to be true that the said Adam Marcham was born a Bastard at the house of a Mr. Vaughan Little New Street Hill in the parish of Saint Brides alias Bridgett in the City of London

Charles Adney aged about 17 years upon his Oath saith that he lived as a hired yearly Servant with Captain Gregory who lived in Fludyer Street for Eighteen Months at the yearly Wages of Thirteen Guineas that his said Master went to Scotland and then returned to England When he went to live at Chiswick that this Examinant for the last Two Months of the greater part of his said Service lived in Sutton Court in the Parish of Chiswick in the County of Middlesex that he has quitted said Service about Seven Months since which time he has done no Act to gain a Subsequent Settlement

Charles Adney Singleman upon his Oath saith that he lived as an hired Yearly Servant for eighteen Months or thereabouts at the Yearly Wages of thirteen Guineas with Captain Gregory that he was discharged from his said Masters Service about Seven Months ago at Chiswick in the County of Middlesex and since then hath gained no other Settlement to the best of his Knowledge

Richard Dobbins One of the Beadles of the Parish of Saint Clement Danes on behalf of Ann George Coleman aged about Six years and John Wm. Coleman aged about Three years Maketh Oath and Saith That he has been informed which Information he verily believes to be true that George Coleman was born a Bastard at the house of a Mr. Butler in Boziers Court Tottenham Court Road in the Parish of Saint Giles in the fields Mary le bone and John Wm. Coleman born at the house of a Mr. Blunk opposite Saint Giles's Church in the said Parish of Saint Giles in the fields in the County of Middlesex both mentioned in the precceding Exaination of George Rochford

Elizabeth Holden Aged about 34 Years or thereabouts Upon her Oath Saith that she intermarried with Edward Holden her present Husband at the Parish Church of Saint Mary le Strand in the County of Middlesex that since their Intermarriage they rented and lived in a House in Lanleys Court in the Parish of Saint Martin in the Fields in the County of Middlesex at a Yearly Rent of upwards of ten Pounds for about two Years that since quitting the said House she does not know of any other Settlement her said Husband has any way acquired and that she this Examinant is poor and unable to maintain herself

Elizabeth Dyke aged about 35 years upon her Oath saith that about Two years ago she Intermarried with Samuel Dyke her present Husband at the Parish Church of Lambeth That her said Husband informed this Examinant which Information she verily believes to be true that he lived as a Yearly Clerk with Brent of Scotland Yard for upwards of Twenty Months that he Rented and lived in Lodgings during such Service in Northumberland Street in the Parish of Saint Martin in the fields in the Liberty of Westminster for Forty days and upwards at the yearly Rent of Ten Pounds and upwards and that after he quitted same he never did to the best of this Examinants knowledge Information or belief Rented any house Tenement or Lodging of Ten Pounds a year paid Taxes or done any Act to gain a subsequent Settlement

Ann Macklin Widow aged 52 years or thereabouts maketh Oath and saith that about six Years ago and since the Decease of her late Husband John Macklin Silk Dyer she lived are hired Yearly Servant with Mr. Darvent at No. 33 in Lawrence Lane in the Parish of Saint Mary le Bow London for the space of Three years and an half together at seven Pounds a Year Wages and since she quitted that Service she hath not lived an hired Yearly Servant for one whole Year together Rented a Tenement or Lodging of Ten pounds a Year Paid any Parish or other Taxes contracted Matrimony or done any Act whatsoever which to her Knowledge or Belief may have gained her a Settlement in any Parish or place

Jane Price Singlewoman aged twenty four Years or thereabouts upon her Oath Saith that she never was married Rented any House or Tenement of the Yearly Value of ten Pounds lived as an hired Yearly Servant for one Year was bound or ever Served as an Apprentice or ever did any Act Matter or thing whereby to acquire any Settlement in her own Right and further this Examinant on her Oath saith that this Examinants late father Thomas Price did in his Life time Rent and live in a House in Whites Alley in the Liberty of the Rolls in the County of Middlesex of the Yearly Value of ten Pounds and upwards for more than forty Days and this Examinant also lived with him aspect of his family there and this Examinant does not know or believe that her said Father nor this Examinant Further since his Dece have either of them acquired any Subsequent Settlement

John Lockton now a Pensioner in the Greenwich Hospital upon his Oath saith that he was married to Jane his present wife at the Parish Church of Saint Botolph without Aldgate in the City of London about 26 Years ago, that he has one Child by his said Wife namely Sarah aged twelve Eight Years or thereabouts who never has acquired any Settlement in her own Right And this Examinant further Saith that sometime ago and whilst he was single and unmarried he lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Mr. Thomas Lancaster who kept the Queens Head Public House in Dark house Lane in the Parish of Saint Mary at hill in the City of London for upwards of one Year that since Quitting his said Service he has not done any other Act Matter or Thing whereby to the best of his Knowledge he may have gained or acquired any subsequent Settlement

Jane Young Widow of Richard Young upon her Oath Saith that in her Husbands Lifetime she and her Husband rented and lived in a House in Gardiners Lane in the Parish of Saint Margaret Westminster at the Yearly Rent of twelve Pounds for upward of forty Days that since quitting such House she has not lived in any other House out of the said Parish of Saint Margaret or rented any House or Tenemt of the Yearly Value of ten Pounds nor done any Act whereby as she best knows and believes she may have acquired a Subsequent Settlement and further this Examinant Saith that she is Sixty four Years of Age or thereabouts and that she is poor and is great Distress and is unable to maintain herself, and has not any Child or Children now living who are any way maintained by by or live with her this Examinant

Ann Jackson widow, of Alphaha Court Stanhope Street in the County of Middlesex and Liberty of Westminster Widow upon her Oath Saith that she has been informed and believes that a Male Infant Child now in the Parish of Saint Clement Danes and deserted by its Parents is the illegitimate Child of Mary Fuller and was born in the Parish of Saint Paul Covent Garden in the County of Middlesex at the House of Mary Doran a Coalshed near the Theatre in Great Russell Street Covent Garden and never has been Christned but is called by the Name of Henry Fuller and this Deponent further Saith that she does not know the Plan of the legal Settlement of the said Mary Fuller nor where the said Mary Fuller now is.

Susannah Bentley of the Parish of Saint Clement Danes in the County of Middlesex upon her Oath saith that she has been informed by Susannah Snowball Widow, and which she believes to be true that the said Susannah Snowball Rented and lived in Apartments in Plough Court Fetter Lane in the Parish of Saint Andrew Holborn in the City of London at the Yearly Rent of ten Guineas for some time that she quitted her said Apartments about two Years ago and since then has not done any Act whereby she may have gained any other or Subsequent Settlement to the best of her Knowledge Information or belief

Francis Bundy of John Street Tottenham Court Road in the Parish of Pancras in the County of Middlesex upon his Oath saith that he was married to Sarah his late Wife at the Parish Church of Saint Dunstan's West in the City of London about two Years ago, and that his said Wife died about four three Months ago, and this Deponent further saith That he has two Children by his said Wife vizt. Ann aged one Year and ten Months or thereabouts and Francis aged three Months or thereabouts who were both of then born in Lawful Wedlock and that his said Wife being dead & he this Examinant being out of Place & Poor he is unable to provide for & Maintain his said two Children who are now with the Person who has Nursed them for since time past in Wych Street in the Parish of Saint Clement Danes in the County of Middlesex and Liberty of Westminster and Chargeable to the said Parish of Saint Clement Danes And this Examinant further on his Oath saith that before his said Intermarriage with his said late wife and whilst he this Examinant was was a singleman not having any Child or Children he lived as an hired Yearly Servant with his Grace the late Duke of Northumberland in the Parish of Saint Martin in the fields for upwards of two Years & that since he quitted the said Dukes Service he has not lived as an hired Yearly Servant for one Year in any Places rented any House or Tenement of the Yearly Value of ten Pounds paid Taxes, served any Parish Office or done any other Act Matter or Thing whereby to the best of his Knowledge Information & belief he may have acquired any subsequent or other Settlement

Sarah Read Widow Aged abt. 50 Years Upon her Oath saith That She was Married to her late Husband John Read at the Parish Church of St. Andrew Holborn about fourteen Years ago, that her Husband sometime abt. the Year 1780, Rented an House in Cow Cross in the parish of St. Sepulchre without , in the County of Middlesex for Six Months or thereabouts which they quitted about Michaelmas in the said Year 1780, since which time he in his life time Nor she this Examinant since her Death have Rented any House or Apartment of £10 Per Year or done any other Act Matter or thing whatsoever whereby to the best of her knowledge Information or belief her said late Husband in his life time or she this Examinant since his Decease might have gained any legal Settlement

Jonathan Peter Mansfield Aged 18 Years or thereabouts upon his Oath Saith That Mathew Mansfield his Father lived a Year and upwds. with a Mr. Powell a Pastry Cook in St. Martins Court in the parish of St. Martin in the Fields in the County of Middlesex that he Served such Year & upwds. as an Apprentice to the sd. Mr. Powell That the sd. Mathew Mansfield his Father has been Dead abt. 5 Yrs. since And this Deponent Examinant Further Upon his Oath Saith that he never lived as a hired Yearly Servant for 1 Yr. Rented any house Tenemt. or Loding for £10. a Yr. or done any Act other Act Matter or thing whereby he might have gained any subsequent Settlement otherwise then by his Fathers serving such time as an Apprentice to the sd. Mr. Powell to this Examinants Knowledge Information or Belief

Ann Ingram Wife of Daniel Ingram Whites Alley in the Liberty of the Rolls Chandler on behalf of her Mother Ann Bedford who now lies Ill at Mr Lightfoots Holler Street in the said parish of Saint Clement Danes Maketh Oath and saith that her Father who Barnaby Bedford (who is now supported by the parish of St. Pancras in their poor House) Rented & lived in an House in Brookes's Garden Tottenham Court Road in the parish of Saint Pancras in the County of Middlesex for abt. Fourteen Years Years at the yearly Rent of £14 which House they quitted abt. 5 Years ago And that her said Mother has informed this Deponent which she verily believes to be true that her said father paid Ten pounds a Year Rent for the same House And this Examinant further saith That her said Father never since Rented any House or Lodging of £10 a year or did any other Act Matter or thing whereby to the best of her knowledge or belief he might have gained any other Settlement And that her said Mother is Ill, Poor and unable to Maintain herself

Deborah Williams Widow Aged 45 Years or thereabouts upon Oath saith That she about twenty five Years ago she intermarried with her late Husband William Richard Williams at the parish Church of St. Botolph Bishopsgate ab who died about 14 Years Since leaving a Son then Aged 4 Years or thereabouts him Surviving, who also Died abt. June the Month of June then Next That during her Widowhood & after the Decease of her said Son she (not having any other Children or Child) lived as an hired yearly Servt . with Mr. Vigne Albion place Surrey side of Blackfriars Bridge in the parish of Christ Church Surry about 17 Months at the Annal Annual Wages of 10 Guineas that she quitted that Service abt. 5 Years ago & since hath not done any Act or thing whereby to the best of her knowledge or belief she may have gained any other legal settlement

Elizth. Edwards Aged 52 Years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith that she was Married to her late Husband John Edwards Deceased at the parish Church of St. Michael in the Town of Cambridge by Banns, in or about the Year 1758 that since then her said Husband Rented & Resided in a House Numbered 7 in Drury Lane in the parish of St Giles in the Fields in the County of Middlesex abt. Six Five Years at the Annual Rent of £12 which they quitted about 20 Years ago since her said Husband in his life time did not do nor has she since his Decease done any Act or thing whatsoever whereby to the best of her knowledge or belief he in his life time or she since might acquire, any legal settlement And saith that she is Poor and unable to maintain herself

Thomas Strode Aged 37 Years or thereabouts Singleman Maketh Oath and saith that he lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Mr. Edward Lloyd in Fenchurch Street in the parish of St Duins Backchurch in the City of London for about 15 Months or upwards at the Yearly Wages of 12 Guineas that he quitted the same Service in the Year 1782 and that since he hath not done any Act or thing whatsoever whereby he might have acquired any Subsequent settlement And that he is Ill Poor and unable to maintain himself

Edward Burbidge one of the Bedles Beadles of the parish of St Clement Danes in the County of Middlesex (for and on behalf of Thomas Pain a Poor Man now lying Ill in the said parish) Maketh Oath and saith that he this Examinant hath been Informed by the Mother of the said Thomas Pain and which he verily believes to be true, that the said Thomas Pain is of the Age of 26 Years of or thereabouts, is the legitimate Son of Samuel and Elizabeth Pain , was Born at the House of Mr.. Clarke's in Vine Street in the parish of St John in the Liberty of Westmr. and County of Middlesex where his said Father & Mother then lodged and Resided, that he hath not not ever done any Act or thing whereby to the best of his Knowledge he might have acquired any legal Settlement in his own Right nor Knows of any settlement he is Intitled unto, (except by Birth as aforesaid) And that he is Poor, Ill and unable to maintain himself

Ann Court Singlewoman Aged 38 Years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Mrs.. Shephard in Dirty Lane Long Acre in the parish of St. Martin in the Fields in the said County and Liberty about two years at the yearly Wages of £5, quitted that Service about 21 Years ago & since hath not since lived as an hired Yearly Servant for 12 Months Rented any House of or Apartment of £10 a Year or done any other Act whatever whereby she might have gained any other legal Settlement to the best of her knowledge or belief And that she is Poor and unable to Maintain herself

Sarah Grant Aged Sixty Years or thereabouts upon her Oath saith that she was Married to her late Husband John Grant at the C a Church or Chapel at Holliston (in that part of Great Britain called Scotland ) according to the Ceremony of the Church of England that her said about 40 years ago, that her said Husband died about twenty Six Years since, that Sher sa she this Examinant after the Death of her said Husband she Rented and Resided in an House in the parish of St. Luke Chelsea in a Street way there called Robinson's Lane , for about two Years at the Annual Rent of £13 that she quitted the said House about twenty years ago that She hath not since Rented any House or Apartment of £10 P a Year, or done any other Act Matter or thing whereby she might have gained any other legal settlement to the best of her knowledges or belief, and that she is Unable to support herself

Thomas Haynes Aged about fifty five years that or thereabouts on his Oath saith that he Married his late Wife Ann Haynes at this parish Church about twenty years ago, that that he rented and lived in an House in the White Hart Yard in the parish of St. Paul Covent Garden in the said Liberty and County about twelve years at the Annual Rent of twelve pounds and twelve Shillings and quitted the same about two years ago, that he hath one Infant Infant Child born of the Body his said late Wife Ann in lawful Matrimony unprovided for Vizt. John Aged about Eleven years, that he hath this Examinant since he quitted the said House in White Hart Yard hath not Rented ten pounds any House or Apartment of Ten pounds a year a Year or done any other Act Matter or thing whatsoever whereby he might have acquired any other legal settlement And that he is Poor and unable to Maintain himself and his said Son

Charlotte Davies Singlewoman Aged twenty three Years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith that she never was Married that she was born in lawful Matrimony at a House in Union Court Holborn where in her late Father David Davis then lodged that he said Father since Rented and lived in a House in Church Yard Court next Fetter Lane next Door to the Black Raven in the parish of Saint Andrew Holborn below the Barrs in the City of London for about two Years at the Annual Rent of £12 that her said Father died there, & after which that her Mother continued to Reside in & occupy'd Rented the said House for upwards of two Months after her ssaid late Father's Decease that her said Mother hath never after did hath done any thing whatever whereby she might have acquired a Subsequent Settlement And this Deponent further saith she never was bound as an Apprentice lived as an hired Yearly Servant or did any Act Matter or thing whereby she might have gained or be intitled unto, any Settlement in her own Right And that she is now is pregnant with a Child or Children And that and is and is now unable to Maintain herself

Elizth Stannenot Aged 17 years upon her Oath saith that she never was Married that she was bound by Indrer by Indres of Apprenticeship to Mrs. Elizth Crisp at No. 73 in Jermyn Street in the parish of St. James Westminster with whom she Regularly served as an Apprentice for four Years and then (being about 4 Months ago) left her said Mistress Service that since she hath not done any Act or thing wtsoever (whereby to the best of her knowledge Information or bele belief) she might have gained any other legal Settlement And that she is Poor and unable to maintain herself

Benjamin Newman one of the Beadles of the said parish of St. Clement Danes in the said County and Liberty (on behalf of Susanna Prickman Widow a Poor Woman now lying Ill at the House of No..18 in Clements Lane in the said parish) Maketh Oath and saith that she the said Susanna Prickman hath Informed this Deponent which he verily believes to be true that she is of the Age of 62 years or thereabouts that about Fifteen years ago she was Married to her late Husband John Prickman at the Parish Church of Wellington Somersetshire that her said Husband died about 2 years since has that he in his life time Rented and with her Resided in a House in Providence Court George Street Grosvenor Square in the parish of Saint George the Martyr Hanover Square in the said Liberty of Westmr. in the said County about 4 years at the Annual Rent of Fourteen Pounds that they quitted the same about three years ago & that he in his Life time did not do nor hath she since his Decease hath not done any Act or thing whereby she might acquire or become intitled unto any Subsequent legal Settlement

Margaret Forrest Aged 22 years old or thereabouts on her Oath saith that on the 12th.. day of January 1790 she intermarried with her present Husband William Forrest at the parish Church of Saint Mary le Strand in the said Liberty and County that her said Husband hath Informed her this Deponent and which she Verily believes to be true that her said Husband was born at the Artichoke in White Hart Yard in the parish of Saint Martin in the Fields in the said Liberty and County and she hath been Informed and believes that her said Husband is an was is an was illegitimate Son and She hath also been that he never lived as an hired yearly Servant for one year or did any other Act or thing whereby in his own Right he might have acquired any legal any any other Subsequent legal Settlement And she farther saith her said Husband is now a Seaman on board His Majesty's Ship the Inconstant and that she is Poor and unable to maintain herself at Court during her lying in

Denis Peakin Aged about thirty Nine years (on behalf of his Mother Margaret Peakin now Ill and Infirm) Maketh Oath and saith that he hath been Informed by his said Mother and verily believes that she his said Mother Margt. Peakin was Married to James Peakin his late Father deced deceased at a Roman Catholic Church or Chapel, in the Town of Kilkenny in the Kingdom of Ireland , about Forty years since, according to the Rights & Ceremony of the Church of Rome that his said Mother about twenty Seven years ago lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr. James Orr a West India Merchant in Great Winchester Street (he believes at the House No.10 there,) in the parish of Alhallows on London Wall in the City of London upwards of one year and that she hath not done any Act Matter or thing whatever (whereby to the best of this Deponents Knowledge or belief) She might have acquired or be intitled unto any subsequent legal Settlement And this Deponent sat saith that he hath never heard from his said Mother or otherwise what Wages she contracted for or Received for such Service with Mr. Orr as aforesaid & that his said Father James Mother Margaret Peakin has been Ill a long time of that the Complaint where with she is Afflicted has entirely so Much disordered her Mental faculties as to under her incapable of Answering (with the least certainty) any Question proposed to her, and that she is Poor and unable to support herself

Catherine Smith Aged about 50 years upon (on the behalf of Patrick King an Infant of the Age of Nine Eight Months & upwards she has been left at this Deponents by his Mother about 4 Months ago) Upon her Oath saith that the said Patrick King is the Son of Patrick King ) and Mary his Wife that she hath been Informed and verily believes to be true that the said Patrick King & Mary his Wife were Married at the Town of Carlisle about 3 Years ago that the said Patrick Rented and with his said Wife Resided in an House called the three Pipes in Dacre Street in the parish of St Margaret in the Liberty of Westmr. and Co. of Middx from the 16th February 1790 to the thirteenth of May then next following, when they quitted and the same & shortly after (before the expiration of the same Month) the said Patrick King the Father went abroad and that Since the said Mary hath not done any Act or thing whereby she might have gained any other legal settlement and this Deponent believes the said Mary King is now at Carlisle and saith that she the said Mary King left the said Child with this Deponent without any Recompence or allow Allowance for supporting the same about four Months ago

Maria Evans Aged 23 Years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith that she lived as an hir never was Married, that she lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Mr Thomas Thomas Cowkeeper & Milkman in Rodney Row at No 6, near the Elephant & Castle in the parish of St. Mary Newington in the County of Surry two Years at the yearly Wages of Six Guineas, that she left that Service about Eight Months ago and since hath not Rented, any House or Apartment of £10 Pr Annum paid any parish Taxes or done any other Act or thing by means whereof she might acquire any legal settlement

John Lamb Aged 42 years or thereabouts upon his Oath said that he intermarried with his late Wife Mary whose Maiden Name was Cunde at the parish Church of St Leonard Shoreditch in the County of Middlesex by Banns about 15 or 16 years ago, that his said Wife died on the 21st. day of October 1788 , that he hath now living two Children Vizt John Aged 7 Years & upwards Mary Aged near 4 years waiting three days she being Born on the 23d. May 1787 both of when were born of the Body of his said late Wife, And this Examinant further saith on his Oath saith that he hath been Informed and verily believes it to be true that his late Father Alexander Lamb was Married to one Ann Simpson this Deponents late Mother at the Fleet but this Deponent has never been informed when such Marriage was Solemnized, that he hath also hath been informed (& which he verily believes to be true) that he this Deponent was Born in a place, then called Sheppard's Market in the parish of St. Geo George the Martyr Hanover Square in the said County And this Deponent further saith that he hath never rented any House or Apartment of £10 a year paid any Taxes severed any parish office or done any other Act or thing whatsoever whereby to obtain any legal legal settlement in his own right that he is so distressed and confined in Circumstance as to render him incapable to support his two Children for whom therefore he is absolutely Necessiated to apply) for Relief

Frances Webb Aged Thirty Years & upwds. upon her Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as an hired yearly Servant with Joseph Williams at the Cock & Crown in Aldersgate Street for Eighteen Months at the yearly Wages of £4, that she immediately afterwards lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr. Robt Band at the Star in Aldg Aldersgate Street Aforesaid for one entire year at the Annual Wages of £5, that both the Houses where she so lived as aforesd aforesaid were situate in the parish of St. Botolph without Aldersgate in the Freedom of the City of London that that And this Deponent saith that she left Mr Band's Service abt. four or Five Years ago and since hath not done any Act or thing whatsoever whereby to gain any legal settlement to the best of her knowledge Information or belief and that she is poor and unable to maintain herself

Ann Green Aged thirty two years and upwards Upon her Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as an hired yearly at Her Majesty's at Buckingham House for one year and upwards at the yearly Wages of Eight Guineas that she was hired by & served as Cook to Mrs Stainforth the then Housekeeper there that during all the time she lived in that that Service she Slept in that a Room in that part of Buckingham House which lies is in the parish of St George the Martyr Hanover Square in the Liberty of Westminster in the County of Middlesex that she left her Maj the Service at Buckingham House befor somtime in the year 1780 and since hath not acquired any legal Settlement whatever And this Examinant further saith that her Male Bastard Child Christened John now of the Ag now of the Age of two twelve Weeks or thereabouts was born of her Body a Bastard on the 8th day of March last at Mr Burton's No 3 in Castle Street Bloomsbury in the parish of St George the Martyr Bloomsbury in the said County and is not yet weaned And this Examinant saith she is Poor and wholly unable to Maintain herself and Child

Mary Perry Aged Sixteen years and upwards upon her Oath saith that she never was Marrie Married nor did any Act Matter or thing whatsoever whereby she may have acquired any legal settlement in her own Right that she her hath heard her late Father James Perry (who died about 15 Months ago) say that he Rented and Resided in a House at the bottom of Princes Street in the parish of St Giles in the Fields in the said County & that he paid Poor Rate for the same during such Occupancy at the Annual Rent of £6 which she verily believes to be true And this Examinant further saith that she perfectly Remembers living with her said Father in the said House and seeing the Officers coming to Collect the Poor Rate and being paid for the same And this Examinant further saith she is poor and unable to maintain herself and that he r never to her knowledge or best belief acquired Subsequent legal settlement

Rose Hannah Broadhead Wife of Matthew Broadhead Aged 49 years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith that she was Married to her present Husband at the Old Church Manchester in the County of Lancaster (by Banns) about on 25th Janry.. 1772 . that since, her said Husband Rented and with her resided in a House No. 92 next the George in Little Drury Lane in the parish of St. Mary le Strand in the said County and Liberty for about 5 or Six years at the Annual Wages Rent of £20, that they quitted the same about four Years ago and since her said Husband has not Rented any House or Apartment of Ten pounds a year or done any other Act Matter or thing whereby he might aquire any legal settlement, that her said Husband left her above has not suffered to be outer put her out of the Apartment wherein he lived on since Monday 30th May last and Refused her living with him again and that she is incapable incapable of supporting herself

Mary Taylor ( Widow of Richard Taylor deced) Aged twenty two years and upwards Maketh Oath and saith That she was Married to her said late Husband Richard Taylor at the parish Church (as she believes) of St. John Clerkenwell in the County of Middlesex abt. 18 Months ago that her said Husband afterwards hath since Rented & with her lived in an House Numbered 35 in Gibraltar Row in the parish of St. George in the Borough of Southwark in the County of Surry about a Quarter of a year at the Yearly Rent of thirteen Guineas that then he when her said Husband Died and that after his Dece she this Deponent Rented the same House & continued to dwell there in for Six Weeks or thereabouts & that then one Chas. Taylor the a Brother of her said late Husband took the said House of her this Examinant & Rented it on his own Acct. and that she since she he so took th & Occupied the said House she this Deponent hath done no Act or thing wtsoever whereby to acquire a Subsequent Settlement And this Examinant further saith she hath an Infant Male Child Named Charles Richard Aged Nine Months or thereabouts born of her bo Body in lawful Matrimony begotten by her said, late Husband who is now with her this Deponent And that she is incapable of maintaining herself and said Child

Elizabeth Barrett Wife of Richard Barrett Aged 44 years or thereabouts Upon Oath saith That abt. Eighteen Years ago she was Married to her present Husband Richd. Barrett at the parish Church of Saint Giles in the Fields in the County of Middlesex That since ther their Marriage her said Husband Rented and with her lived in an Apartment in an House in Portsmouth Street next the Black Jack in the parish of St Giles aforesaid in the Fields , aforesaid in the Said County of Middlesex for Ten Years or thereabouts at the Yearly Rent of £18 that they quitted the said same House about Ten Years ago And that since her said Husband quitted the said Apartment he hath not to the best of her knowledge or belief done any Act or thing whatsoever whereby to obtain a Subsequent Settlement And that her said Husband as this Examinant has been informed and believes) now lives in the Service of Thos Grace the the present Lord Lientenant of the Kingdom of Ireland And lastly that Examinant is incapable of providing for herself

Mary Burgess Aged 25 years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith That she was Married to her present Husband Edward Burgess at Christ Church in the County of Surry on the 27th Day of August 1787 . by Barnes That previous thereto and while he was single not having any Child or Children her said Husband lived as an hired Yearly Clerk or Servant with Messrs. Sandom & Co. in America Square John Street Minories for two Years or thereabouts at the Wages of Fifty pounds for the first, and Sixty pounds for the second Year, that during the last three or four Months of such Service he lodged and constantly slept in the House of Mr Beridge at Newington Cause way in the Parish of St. Mary Newington in the County of Surry That he left the Service of Messrs. Sandom & Co. about four or five years ago and since hath not done any Act or thing whatsoever to acquire or whereby he might be entitled unto any other legal Settlement That she hath one Child now living with her born of her Body (in legal Matrimony) and be gotten by her said Husband Named Edward Aged 20. One Year Eight Months or thereabouts, And that her said Husband is now with his own Friends, Dangerously Ill and that she is Poor and unable to provide for herself and said Child;

Robt. Jackson Aged Nineteen years & upwards Upon his Oath saith that he never was Married that he lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Mr. Swyffin at the Talbot as Spotted Dog Tottenham Court Road in the parish of St. Pancras in the said County and Liberty abt. 13 Months at the Yearly Wages Rent of £5 that he quitted that Service abt. thirteen Months ago and since then hath not done any Act or thing wtsoever whereby to his knowledge or belief he might acquired any other legal Settlement and that he is Ill Poor & unable to support himself

James Talboys one of the Beadles of the parish of St. Clement Danes in the said County & Liberty (on behalf of Sarah Smith Widow Aged 65 years or thereabouts now very) Jufirm) Maketh Oath and saith that he hath been informed and verily believes to be true that the said Sarah Smith intermarried at the parish Church of St. George in the East in the said County of Middlesex about thirty years ago with her late Husband Wm. Smith who died about 20 years ago leaving no Issue by the Sarah Smith him Surviving that after his Decease being Single & not having any Child or Children she lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Messrs Phillips & Small Upholsterers in Piccadilly in the parish of St. James in the Liberty of Westminster near the same parish Church Six Years and upwards at £7 & 10s Yearly Wages that she left the same about Twelve Years ago & that since she hath not (by any means whatever) to the best as her knowledge acquired any legal Settlement

Elizabeth Holborn Aged 45 years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith That she was Married to her present Husband Thomas Holborn about Nine or Ten years ago that since their at the Parish Church of Saint Olave in the Borough of Southwark in the County of Surry (by Banns) that sence that the time of her saith Intermarriage her said Husband Rented and with her Resided in an House Numbered 11. Vine Street in the parish of Saint Martin in the Fields in the said Liberty an and County about One year at the Annual Rent of £16 or upwards that her said Husband quitted that House in or about November or December last and that since he so quitted the said House he hath not (by any way or means whatever) acquired any other legal Settlement to this Deponent's Knowledge or belief and this Deponent further on her Oath saith that her said Husband is now in the Workhouse belonging to the said parish of St. Martin in the Fields , and that she is Poor and incapable of providing for herself

John Roberts Aged 54 years or thereabouts Upon his Oath saith That he abt. 11 Years ago, he Intermarried with his present Wife Elizabeth at the parish Church of St. Leonard Shoreditch by whom he has no Issue & with whom he does not now, Cohabit neither has he for two Years past, that about Twenty two Years ago he hired an House then caller the George & Harp in the Old Bailey in the parish of St. Sepulchre within the City of London & that he Rented and Resided therein for two years and three Months or thereabouts at the Annual Rent of £45. and that since he hath not (by any means whatever) acquired any other legal Settlement and that he is Ill Poor and unable to maintain himself

Res Catherine Rossat Wife of Ferdinand Rossat Aged 22 years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith that about five Months ago she intermarried with her present Husband Ferdinand Rossat at the parish Church of St James in the Liberty of Westminster in the County of Middlesex That Previous thereto and while he was single and unmarried not having Child or Children he hired was living as an hired himself as an a Yearly Servant in the capacity of Usher to Mr. Freselion Love Lane in the parish of Wandworth in the County of Surry sometime in the spring or beginning of the summer of the 1790 at the yearly income or Wages of £25 and so continued to live with his said Marte till about 24th June now last when he quitted such service that he bearded and lodged all the time at his said Master's House during his continuance with him and since has not acquired any subsequent legal Settlement And further on her Oath saith that her said Husband Deserted and left her destitute on Friday last and she has not where with and is at present unable to maintain herself.

Eleanor De Fereand Wife of William De Fereand Aged 39 years or thereabout Upon her Oath saith that her Mother Elizabeth Watson is now living with this Deponent of the Age of Sixty years or thereabouts, now Infirm as well Mentally as Bodily, that she in the wife of Richard Watson new in the Workhouse belonging to the parish of St. Giles Chipplegate in the Liberty and Freedom of the City of London that this Depont. hath been informed and believed that her said Mother & her said Husband were Married at the parish Church of St Luke in the County of Middlesex on or about the 19th day of November 1760 that the said Richd Watson While was bound by Indenture of Appren ticeship to a John Priest Citizen & Brass Founder of Greek Street in the parish of St Giles's Cripplegate ale London Resident in the parish of St Giles Cripplegate in the Liberty of the said City and regularly served his Apprenticeship And that since he hath not Gained any subsequent legal Settlement as this Deponent hath been informed and believed and that her said Mother is now unable support herself

Elizabeth Walker Aged 35 years or thereabouts Widow of Thomas Walker Maketh Oath and saith that about Seventeen years ago she was Married to her said late Husband Thomas Walker at the parish Church of Saint Clement Danes in the said County and Liberty that previous thereto, while he was single and unmarried not having any Child or Children he lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Mr. Edward Hitchiner in the parish of Hitchin in the County of Herlford for about 3 or 4 years as he informed this Deponent and which she believes to be true; that he quitted the said Edward Hitchiner s as the and came immediately to William Hitchiner 's Esquire which she thinks was about Eighteen or Nineteen years that since their said Marriage her said Husband Rented and with her Resided in an unfurnished Apartment in Crown Street otherwise Hogg Lane in the parish of St Giles in the Fields in the said County of Middlesex for Six Months at the yearly Wages Rent of Ten Guineas that they said left the same about Nine years ago and that since her said Husband in his life time not hath this Examinant since his Decease (by any way or means to her knowledge or belief) acquired any other legal Settlement

John Ashton Aged 38 years or thereabouts Upon Oath saith that he never was Married that he was bound an Apprentice by with the Consent of his Father John Ashton to John Grace Cross Court Russell Court in the parish of St. Martin in the Fields in the said Liberty and County for Seven years and duly Served the whole of his said time lodging & Sleeping at his said Masters House And this Examinant saith that since his said Apprenticeship expired he hath not (by any means whatever) acquired any other legal settlement And that he is Poor and unable at present to maintain himself

Margaret Colder Aged 51 years or thereabouts Upon Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as an hired Yearly Servant with Mr. Clifford a Groom in the Kings Mews in the parish of St Martin in the Fields Middx about Sixteen Months at the Annual Wages of five pounds-that she quitted the same about Sixteen or Eighteen Years ago & since hath not done any Act or thing whatever whereby she might have acquired any other legal Settlement than in the said parish of St Martin in the Fields And that she in Poor and unable to maintain herself

Mary Gilmour Aged 22 years & upwards upon her Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as an is the legitimate Daughter of John Gilmour and Mary his late Wife -that her said Father Rented and Resided in a House Situate in Lumby's Court in the parish of St. Martin in the Fields in the Liberty of Westminster & Co of Middx about two years at the Annual Rent of £12 or upwards that he quitted the same about 4 or 5 years ago and since hath not (by any) means) Acquired any legal Settlement that she this Deponent hath never been bound or served as an Apprentice hath never lived as on hired yearly Servant for a twelve month under one hiring nor done any other Act Matter or thing Whereby she might acquire any legal Settlement in her own Right

Mary Marshfield Aged 54 years or thereabouts (on behalf of John Eades with whom she has Cohabited for 18 years or thereabouts but to whom she was never legally Married) Upon her Oath saith that the said John Eades while he was Single & unmarried not having any Child or Children lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr. Bullock a Cook in South Audley the Corner of Green Street in the parish of St George Hanover Square in the said Liberty of Westminster & County of Middlesex about 2 years & an half at the year Wages of 30s for the first & 40d the second year that he quitted the as he hath Informed her this Deponent & which she verily believes to be true And he hath also Informed this Examinant which she verily believes to be true That he Since he quitted the same (which he hath been told was when he was about the Age of twelve years) he hath not rented any House or Apartment of ten pounds, a year served as an hired yearly Servant or done any other Act whereby he might obtain any Subsequent legal Settlement to the best of her knowledge or belief with at he is now Poor & dangerously Ill

Benjamin Newman of the Beadles of the said parish of St Clement Danes and behalf of Susanna Bingley Widow Maketh Oath & saith that she the said Susanna Bingley hath Informed him this Deponent & he verily believes it to be true that she rented & Resided in a House in Royal Row in the parish of St Mary Lambeth in the County of Surry for two years or thereabouts at the Yearly Rent of £16..16..0 and paid the Poors Rate for the same that she quitted the same in or about the Month of June 1790 and that she since hath not done any Act Matter or thing since whereby to obtain any other legal Settlement to the best of her knowledge or belief And this Deponent saith that she is now very Infirm & Lame

Benjamin Newman one of the Beadles of the Parish of St. Clement Danes abovementd on behalf of Jane lake Widow now Ill and fired to her Room Maketh Oath and Saith that she the said Jane Lake hath Informed this Depont. which he verily believes to be true that she Intermarried with her present Husband Wm. Lake at the parish Church of St Paul Convent Garden about 15 years ago that she is now of the Age of 46 years as thereabouts that since then said Marriage her said Husband Rented and with her Rented in an House in Well Street Oxford Road in the parish of St. May le bone in the Courts of Middlesex about two years at and under the Annual Rent of £18. that they quitted the same about four years ago and since that her said Husband hath not done any Act where by to obtain any Subsequent legal Settlement that her said Husband left her about three weeks ago and she doth not known where he now is and that she is Ill & Poor

Mary Burgess Aged 29 years or thereabouts Upon her Oath saith that she Intermarried with her late Husband at the parish Edward Burges at Christ Church in the Co. of Surry on the 27th. day of August 1787 by Banns That previous there to and while he her said Husband Edward Burges was single and unmarried not having any Child or Children he lived as an hired yearly Servt. or Clerk with Messrs. Sanderman & Graham in America Square John Street Minories for two years together at the Wages of Fifty pounds for the first and Sixty pounds for the second year that during part of his said service he lived lodged & slept with Mr Burdett No.1 Old Change in the parish of St. Michael Queen in the City of London Glazier at the lu upwards of two Months and that he quitted the same sometime in October 1785 as she verily believes & in the November succeeding he left the Service of Messrs. Sanderman & Co. And hath not since in his life time after quitting the sd Mr. Burdett done any Act Matter or thing whereby to obtain any Subsequent legal settlement to the best of her knowledge or belief that she hath one Child Named Edward Aged two years who was begotten by her said Husband and is the her only Surviving Child - And that is unable to Maintain herself & Child without some Relief And their said Husband is now Dead as she is Informed & Newly belives

J, the undersigned being one of the overseers of the poor of the Parish of Saint Clement Danes , do hereby undertaken that the Mary day the pauper named in this Examination shall not be removed for the parish of Saint Clement Danes by Virtued the Orders signed on this Examination until she is adjudged to be able to bear such removal Josa Johnston Benjamin Newman one of the Beadles of the Parish of Saint Clement Danes in the Liberty of Westminster & County of Middlesex Maketh oath and Saith, That he hath been informed, and which Information he verily believes that Mary Day widow aged Sixty five Years or thereabouts who is now week and infirm and lodges in Nogs Head Court in the Parish of Saint Clement Danes aforesaid at the House of one Mrs. Davis there and that she the said Mary Day togr- with her late Husband Rented and lived in a House in Hoxton in the Parish of Saint Leonard Shoreditch in the Co: of Middlesex at the Yearly Rent of twelve Pounds, that they for four or five Years, that they quitted the Same about ten Years ago, and since then the said Mary Day hath not gained any Subsequent Settlement other by Renting any Tenement of the Yearly Value of ten pounds or other and that the Husband of the said Mary Day died at the House above mentioned in Hoxton aforesaid

Catherine Glover aged thirty three Years or thereabouts upon her Oath saith that she was married to Thomas Glover her present Husband at the Parish Church of Saint Martin in the Fields in the County of Middlesex on the 26th Day of Sept 1785 - that after their Intermarriage they Rented & hired for about three Months in a House in Charles Long Ann in the Parish of Saint in the Fields at the Rent of £24 P Ann & that since thing the said House neither her said Husband nor herself have done any Act Matter thing whereby to the last of her knowledge Information and belief her said Husband or herself may have acquired any or subsequent Settlement and this Deponent further saith that the hath one Child now living by her said Husband Namely Elizabeth aged five Years or thereabouts and that her said Husband hath deserted & Refuses to Maintain her and her said Child and she this Deponent in poor and out of Work and in great Distress for necessaries to maintain and provide for herself and said Child

Elizth. Dellett on the behalf of Sarah Briggs her Child Aged upwards of 9 Years upon her Oath Saith that she intermarried was Chas. Briggs her late Husband about 16 Years Ago at the parish Church of Saint Clement Danes by same that she has had 5 Children by him which one all dead but the said Sarah Briggs Who hath never gained any Settlement in her own Right That her said Husband was bound Apprentice and duly Served the whole of his time to William Briggs his Father of Bedford Court in the Parish of Saint Martin in the Fields in the County of Middlesex Waterman That her said Husband since he served his said Apprenticeship has never Rented any Tenement or Lodging of Ten pounds a Year lived as a hired Yearly servant paid Taxes or done any other Act to gain any Subsequent Settlement And this Examinant further Upon her Oath saith that she between 2 and 3 Years Ago she intermarried with James Dellett at the Chapal of Gosport in this parish of Alverstoke who is now living And that during the time she Remained a Widow (re) from the decease of her said Husband Chas Briggs to the intermarriage with the said James Dellett she never Rented any Tenement or Lodging of £10 a Year lived as a hired Yearly Servants did any other Act Matter or thing to the best of her knowledge information or belief whereby the said Sarah Briggs her said Child might have gained any other Settlement but by the Fathers Serving his Apprenticeship as aforesaid that through Sickness & misfortunes she this Examinant is Poor and unable to maintain her said Child and hath therefore been obliged to make application to the

Elizabeth Sawyer on the behalf of Elizabeth Constantia Sawyer her Child Aged about 13 Months upon her Oath Saith that the said Elizth. Conta. Sawy her Child was born at the House of a Mr. Richardson Situate on the Road Side near the Elephant & Castle in the parish of Saint Pancras in the County of Middlesex that she is the Illegit Child of this Examinant she this Examinant having never been Married And this Examinant further Saith that the said Child is now at nurse with Mr. Wood 2:9 Strand Lane in the parish of Saint Clement Danes in the County of Middlesex - And she this Examinant in Poor and unable to maintain her said Child

Catherine Jiles aged about 24 Years Upon her Oath saith that she never was Married That she was Born in Chamber where her Father and Mother Rented and lived in a House in Chamber Street where Goodman Fields in the parish of Saint Mary Whitechapel in the County of Middlesex where she this Examinant was Born That her said Father and Mother has been Dead upwards of 6 Years That soon after their Death she this Examinant was taken by as a Servant by a Mr. Ridley in Chamber Street aforesaid in the said Parish of Saint Mary Whitechapel and lived there upwards of 4 Years but was not hired as a Yearly Servant as she this Examinant was generally said Weekly And further Saith that since the quitted said Service she has Lodged in the Wych Street in the said parish of Saint Clement Danes And further Saith that she never lived as a hired Yearly servant for One Year Rented any Tenement or Lodging of £10. a Year paid Taxes or done any Act Matter or thing whereby she might have gained any Subsequent Settlement to the best of this Examinants Knowledge information or belief,

Robert Harris Aged 56 years on thereabouts upon Oath saith that he is the Son of John and Tobitha Harris that he hath been told his father that his Father in his Life time time Rented & lived in an House called then known by the Sign of the Rainbow & Dove in the Minories in the parish of St Botolp without Aldgate London but what rent his said father paid for the same or how long he kept & resided in the same this Deponent hath never been Informed that his sd. Mother hath also Informed this Deponent that his said father served his Apprenticeship under Indentures in the Minories in the said parish of St Botolph Aldgate and that since his said father or Mother never have gained any subsequent legal Settlement - And this Deponent further on his Oath saith that he perfectly remembers his said Mother was supported by the said parish of St. Botolph that he never acquired any settlement in his own right and that he is poor & unable to support himself

Elizabeth Glenn Singlewoman Aged 27 years or thereabouts on behalf of John Jenkins Aged 37 years & upwards now very Ill upon Oath saith That she hath been Informed by him the said John Jenkins that he is of the Age of 37 years and upwards that while he was single and unmarried he was Articled to Mr. Boyden Haw Daeper King Street in the parish of St Margaret Westminster for 7 years and secured his said Master the whole Term that the last forty days of his said Service he lodged in the Broad Sanctuary in the said parish of St Margaret and hath since done no Act whereby to obtain any Subsequent legal Settlemt. and that he is sick Poor and unable to maintain himself

Elizth Glenn Singlewoman Aged 27 years or thereabouts Upon Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as an hired Yearly toward Servant with Mr. Leach No. 15 Great Suffolk Street in the parish of St Martin in the fields in the Liberty of Westminster at the yearly Wages of £8.8s that she quitted that Service only about 3 Weeks ago and hath not acquired not acquired any Subsequent legal Settlemts - Child that she is now Poor and unable to maintain herself

Frances Rogers Aged 39 years or thereabouts upon Oath saith that she never was Married that she lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr. Ralph Potts at No. 5 in Huggins Alley in the parish of St. John's Lachary in the City of London for about one three one year & three Months at the yearly Wages of five Pounds but this Examinant never received more than two pounds as her Master was Insolvent & much distressed, that she quitted her said Service in the Month of May last and since has not rented ten pounds a year paid any Taxes or done any other Act Matter or thing to obtain any other legal settlement

Catherine Forrest Aged 35 years or thereabouts Upon Oath saith that She never was Married that she lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr. Fossett Taylor in Maiden Lane in the parish of St. Paul Covent Garden in the Liberty of Westminster and County of Middlesex for Eighteen Months at the Yearly Wages of £5 - that she left such Service abt. the End of the year 1782 or beginning of the year 1783 and since has not lived as an hired yearly Servant, Rented any House or Apartment of £10 Pr. Annums paid any parish Taxes or otherwise acquired any other legal Settlement And she is now distress and unable to maintain maintain herself

Mary Price Singlewoman Aged 58 years & upwards Upon Oath saith that she never was Married, that she lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr. Day Trunk Maker in Cateaton Street, the Corner of Lawrence Lane in the parish of St Lawrence Jewry in the City of London about upwards of thirteen Months at the Annual Wages of £7., that she quitted that Service about Six years ago and since hath not lived as an hired yearly Servt. for one year together and or one hiring hiring, Rented any House or Apartment of ten pounds a year paid parish Taxes or otherwise acquired any legal Settlement (except as in the parish of St Lawrence Jewry aforesaid) And that she is now unable to maintain herself without some relief

Henry Lewis Aged 53 years & upwards Upon his Oath saith that he did about Seventeen or Eighteen years ago intermarried with Hannah his late Wife where Maiden Name was Griffiths at the parish Church of Saint Martin in the Fields - that his said Wife Died on or about the 22d of November 1789 . that previous thereto and while he was to his said Marriage being single and not having any Child or Children he lived as an hired yearly Servant for about years at the three years at the Annual Wages of £25 with Mr. Henry Deale who then resided at the Corner of Brook Street Holborn in the parish of St. Andrew Holborn below the Bars in the Liberty of the City of London and during the whole of the last year he slept in his said Master Apartment which was situate in the same parish and within the said Liberty that he quitted his said Master's Service about the year 1767 or 1768 and since hath not obtained any other legal settlement and that he is at present unable to maintain himself without Assistance

Ann Macklin Widow Aged 53 years or thereabouts Upon Oath saith that about Six years ago and since the Decease of her late Husband John Macklin Silk Dyer (to whom she was married at St Clement Danes Church in the strand near 21 years ago) she lived as an hired yearly Servant with Mr. Dawen at No. 38 in Lawrence Lane in the parish of St. Martin le bow London for the space of three year & an half together at Seven pounds a year Wages, and since she quitted that Service she hath not hired lived as an hired yearly Servant for one whole year together Rented a Tenement or Lodging of £10 a year paid any parish Taxes contracted Matrimony or done any Act Matter whatsoever which upon knowley or belief may have gained her a settlement in the parish or place And this Deponent further said that she was removed by Orders of Removal from the parish of St Clement Danes be the said parish of St. Mary Le Bow London in or about December last and or the settlement by the service aforesaid and was Maintained with their poor at Hoxton in the County of Middlesex about five Months to which Order of Removal they have not at any time appealed and that she is unable to provide for herself without some Assistance and has therefore applied to the said parish of St. Mary le bow for Relief which they have refused without She some legally passed

Mary Blackbird James Talboys one of the Beadles of the parish of St Clement Danes aforesaid on behalf of Mary Blackbird Widow of Maketh Oath and saith that the said Mary Blackbird hath Informed servt which he verily believes & that about 40 years ago or refused she intermarried with her late Husband John James Blackbird at the Chapel of St. John Wapping then belongg. to the Chapelay of and belonging to the parish Church of St. Dunstan Stepney in the County of Middlesex That after their said Marriage her said late Husband Rented and with her Resided in an House House situate in Grays Inn Lane in the parish of St. Andrew Holborn above the Bars in the sd. County for about 4 years at and under the Annual Rent of £14 that they quitted the same about twenty five years ago and since her said Husband in his Life time and not gain nor hath he this Examinant the said Mary Blackbird since his Decease acquired any other Subsequent legal Settlement- and that she hath farther Informed this Deponent which he verily believes to be true that only about 8 Weeks she was aclieved as a Pensioner belonging to the said parish and so had been for same time then past - And that she is unable to maintain herself

Ann Finch widow Aged 38 years thereabouts Upon Oath saith that about Sixteen years ago she was Married to her late Husband Thomas Finch at the parish Church of St. Mary Lambeth since their Marriage her said Husband Rented and with her Resided in an Apartment in the House the Corner Round Court in the street in the parish of St Martin in the Fields with Liberty of Westminster in the said County for about two Years and an half at the yearly Rent of Ten pounds and ten Shillings that the same Apartments during all the said Term was hired as an furnished and furnished by this Deponent said Husband that her said Husband served his Apprenticeship at he hall Intermarried this Deponent with Mr. Hurst in Hedge Lane in the said parish of St. Martin in the fields with whom he ledged the whole that she this Deponent hath been in the Workhouse belonging to and been relieved by the said parish that she was in the said Workhouse only so lately as about twelve Months ago that her Child and that her said Husband in his Life time had not nor hath she since his Decease acquired any other subsequent others legal Settlement than by Renting the said Apartment in round Court as aforesaid

Benjamin Newman one of the Beadler of the parish of St. Clement Danes . in the said County Liberty on behalf of Elizth. Eldin Aged thirty Nine years or thereabouts Maketh Oath & saith that she the said Elizabeth Eldin hath Informed this Deponent which he verily believes to be time that he never was married that she lived as an hired yearly Servant with Shr. Mr. Lane at Cecil Street Coffee House in the Strand in the parish of St. Martin in the Fields in the Liberty of Westminster in the County of Middlesex aforesaid for about three years at the annual Wages of £10..10..0 that she quitted the same about four Years ago & hath not since (by any way or means wt soever) obtained any Subsequent legal settlement And this Deponent saith that she is now Ill poor & (as he is Informed) Pregnant with an illegitimate Child or Children

Mary Oglivie Singlewoman aged about 25 years Upon her Oath saith that she never was Married never lived as an hired Yearly Servant For a Twelve month together under one hiring, served as an Apprentice, Rented any House or Apartment of £10 a year, paid Parochial Taxes, or otherwise obtained any legal Settlement in her own Rights, That her Father Thomas Ogilvie 's (as he hath Informed this Deponent which she verily believes to be true) Intermarried with his late a Wife this Deponent's late another Sophia at the parish Church of St. Andrew Holborn about thirty years ago That since then her said Father Rented & lived in a House in King Street the parish of St. Giles in the fields in the County of Middlesex for about four or five years at the Annual Rent of Eighteen or twenty pounds that he quitted the same about thirteen years ago since hath not (anywise obtained any other legal Settlement and this Examinant further upon Oath saith that she was removed by Orders of Removal from the said Parish of St. Clement Danes to the said Parish of St. Giles in the Fields in or about the Month of May 1789 against which Orders they never Appealed-that she was maintained for a fortnight or upwards in the Workhouse belonging to the said parish of St Giles at the time she was removed by Virtue of such Orders

Mary Golston wife of John Golston Aged 45 Years or thereabouts Upon Oath saith that she was Married to her present Husband John Golston at the Chapel in Kentish Town in the County of Middlesex about Nine years ago that her said Husband served as an Apprentice under Indentures with Mr. Thomas Norton at Turnham Green in the parish of Chiswick in the said County for about 5 years that at the Expiration of that Term he left his Master without his consent or pervity went to sea in the Service of His Majesty and or the Reynolds in that her said Husband hath never gained any subsequent legal Settlement and this Deponent farther saith that this Deponent's said Husband hath left this Deponent about Eight days and age and where has ago but where or on what occasion he is gone this Deponent known not And saith that about 14 Months ago this Deponent together with her said Husband werd Removed by Orders of Removal from the Liberty of the Rolls in the said County to Chiswick aforesaid and were by Virtue of the said Orders taken into the Workhouse and maintain at the charge of the said parish of Chiswick for about five Months again against which Orders of Removal there has been no Appeal to this Deponents knowledge or belief as theywere never Returned from that parish to the Liberty of the Rolls aforesaid And Lad by this Deponent saith that she is now distressed and unable to maintain herself witht. Assistance
